Claim 1 (Currently amended): An alarm system comprising: a physiological monitor capable of triggering a first alarm in response to an alarm condition; and a station located remotely from the physiological monitor, wherein the station is capable of receiving an input from the physiological monitor and triggering a second alarm in response to the alarm condition, and wherein when the second alarm is not acknowledged within a predetermined time period, the station is capable of sending an output to the physiological monitor to initiate an escalated alarm at the physiological monitor, wherein the escalated alarm is __perceptually distinct from the first alarm__.

Claim 2 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the second alarm is capable of being acknowledged by an operator input before expiration of a timer.

Claim 3 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm comprises an inaudible alarm.

Claim 4 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm.

Claim 5 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm comprises an audible alarm and the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm that is louder than the first alarm.

Claim 6 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm and the second alarm are triggered substantially simultaneously.

Claim 7 (Previously presented): The system of claim 1, wherein the station located remotely from the physiological monitor is part of a central patient management system.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The system comprising: a processor programmed to trigger an alarm in response to an alarm condition; a memory capable of storing alarm data associated with the alarm, wherein the alarm data comprises an alarm type, a time that the alarm was triggered, __and an escalation status__; and a display capable of displaying the alarm data, wherein the system is __integrated with a physiological monitor or a central management system and is capable of receiving alarm condition data from the physiological monitor__.
